prompt: A new implementation gets B’s final count right. Which check would expose an accidental reset between the two cycles?

options.text: Count the four NS and four EW arrivals across all 16 slots.
options.feedback: A reset discards waiting vehicles. The incoming traffic can still add up exactly as specified.

options.text: Look for an NS departure at slot 9, when the only arrivals are EW.
options.feedback: That departure uses one of the two NS vehicles carried from slot 8. A reset would leave nobody to depart on this green, yet B could still finish with two vehicles.

options.text: Compare the last row of each independent eight-slot B run.
options.feedback: Independent runs each start empty and each end with two NS vehicles. They leave the handoff between the cycles untested.

prompt: The spreadsheet’s author confirms that 20 counts vehicles. Which follow-up would establish whether it belongs beside B’s slot-16 result?

options.text: Check whether both files were exported on the day the model was run.
options.feedback: An export date can help locate a source. It cannot identify which queues were counted, under which conditions or when the count was taken.

options.text: Check whether the model accepts a queue of 20 as a valid whole number.
options.feedback: Twenty is a possible count, but checking the value’s format leaves its meaning and origin unresolved.

options.text: Recover which queues were counted, when, and under which input conditions and configuration.
options.feedback: With those details and the input conditions, a reviewer can judge whether both records measure the same quantity under comparable conditions.

prompt: A requirement limits detector-to-controller delivery time while diagnostics share the physical link. Which run would let the reviewer assess that requirement for the proposed configuration?

options.text: Use the intended devices and link under the specified load. Measure from send to receipt.
options.feedback: The measured interval and load match the requirement. Recording the device revisions, link settings and clock basis lets the reviewer relate the result to this configuration.

options.text: Run the receiver software under the specified load. Measure how long it spends processing each delivered report.
options.feedback: That run could identify a processing bottleneck. Its clock starts after delivery, so it misses the interval the requirement limits.

options.text: Use the intended devices and link with diagnostics paused. Measure from send to receipt.
options.feedback: This would give an unloaded baseline. The requirement concerns competition for the link, so the reviewer needs a run with the declared diagnostic traffic.
